name: Idaho
note: An Idaho death is reported twice. Within 24 hours of taking possession, the mortician files a written report with the local registrar that serves as the in-state burial permit. Within five days the death certificate itself is filed with the local registrar, who sends it on to the state registrar. The attending physician, PA or APRN certifies cause within 72 hours; the county coroner certifies unattended or non-natural deaths and must authorise every cremation. Since 2025, Health and Welfare must send the Secretary of State a monthly list of residents who died, for county clerks to cancel their voter registrations.

citations.title: Registration of deaths and stillbirths
citations.quote: A certificate of each death which occurs in this state shall be filed with the local registrar of the district in which the death occurs

citations.title: Registration of deaths -- five-day deadline
citations.quote: or as otherwise directed by the state registrar, within five (5) days after the occurrence.

citations.title: Registration of deaths -- person responsible
citations.quote: The person in charge of interment or of removal of the body from the district shall be responsible for obtaining and filing the certificate.

citations.title: Registration of deaths -- medical certification
citations.quote: who shall certify to the cause of death according to his best knowledge, information and belief within seventy-two (72) hours from time of death

citations.title: Registration of deaths -- referral to coroner
citations.quote: refer the following cases to the coroner who shall make an immediate investigation, supply the necessary medical data, and certify to the cause of death

citations.title: County coroner to investigate deaths
citations.quote: When a county coroner is informed that a person has died, the county coroner shall investigate that death if:

citations.title: Authorization for final disposition -- report within 24 hours
citations.quote: shall make a written report to the registrar of the district in which death or stillbirth occurred

citations.title: Authorization for final disposition -- cremation and removal
citations.quote: If the body is to be cremated, the coroner must also give additional authorization.

citations.title: Transmittal of certificates and local records
citations.quote: Local registration officers shall transmit all certificates filed with them to the state registrar in accordance with the regulations of the board.

citations.title: Duties of state registrar
citations.quote: Be official custodian of all its files and records

citations.title: Disclosure of information -- copies
citations.quote: may be issued to any applicant who can show direct and tangible interest in the record for which he applies

citations.title: Disclosure of information -- child support and fraud
citations.quote: to a state, federal or local public agency for child protection and child support enforcement purposes or for the purpose of investigation of fraud

citations.title: Disclosure of information -- verification of data
citations.quote: data contained on records may be used by federal, state or municipal agencies for the purpose of verification of data

citations.title: Disclosure of information -- no public lists
citations.quote: No lists of registration shall be compiled for public use, except as provided in section 34-433

citations.title: Disclosure of information -- public after 50 years
citations.quote: fifty (50) years have elapsed after the date of death, stillbirth, marriage or divorce

citations.title: Fee for copies, searches and other services -- death certificates
citations.quote: the national agency in charge of vital statistics may obtain copies or certifications of data from records without payment of fees

citations.title: Penalties -- misdemeanours
citations.quote: transporting, accepting for transport, interring, or otherwise disposing of a dead body or stillborn fetus without a permit or other authorization

citations.title: Penalties -- fine for late signature
citations.quote: fails to sign a birth, or death or stillbirth certificate within fifteen (15) days of the death

citations.title: Accuracy of voter registration information -- monthly death list
citations.quote: the legal name, date of birth, county of residence, and residence address of each Idaho resident who has died during the preceding month

citations.title: Accuracy of voter registration information -- county cancellations
citations.quote: county clerk shall immediately review the information and initiate cancellations of all registrations of individuals reported as deceased or determined to be ineligible to vote

citations.title: Registration of deaths and stillbirths -- acceptance of incomplete death certificate
citations.quote: must file the certificate as prescribed by the State Registrar with all information that is available

steps.title: Coroner cases referred to the county coroner
steps.who: The person in charge of interment or removal of the body (any person informing the coroner).
steps.trigger: No attending practitioner in the last illness, circumstances suggesting a non-natural death, or no available certifier; and the listed coroner cases (homicide, suicide, accident, drugs, custody, unattended death, and others).
steps.summary: The coroner investigates immediately, supplies the medical data and certifies the cause. It must investigate the listed categories of death, with law enforcement doing any criminal investigation.

steps.title: Best-qualified person supplies personal data
steps.who: The person best qualified to supply them (usually next of kin).
steps.summary: Personal data on the certificate are supplied, over their signature, by the person best qualified to give them.

steps.title: Attending practitioner certifies cause of death
steps.who: The physician, physician assistant or advanced practice registered nurse who attended the last illness; or an associate, the institution's chief medical officer, or the autopsy physician for a natural death.

deadline.text: within 72 hours from time of death

steps.summary: The attending practitioner certifies the cause of death. If the certificate is filed without it under the hardship rule, the certification must reach the vital statistics unit within 15 days. The registrar may fine a certifier who fails to sign within 15 days.

steps.title: Coroner certifies cause in referred cases
steps.summary: The coroner supplies the medical data and certifies the cause of death.

steps.title: Mortician's 24-hour report to the local registrar serves as in-state burial permit
steps.who: The mortician or person acting as such who first takes possession of the body.

deadline.text: within 24 hours after taking possession of the body

steps.summary: The written report, with confirmation that the attending practitioner will sign, is the permit to transport, bury or entomb within Idaho. It is not enough for removal from the state, cremation or coroner cases, which need an authorisation for final disposition from the certifier; cremation also needs the coroner's authorisation.

steps.title: Death certificate filed with the local registrar
steps.who: The person in charge of interment or of removal of the body from the district.

deadline.text: within five days after the death

steps.summary: The certificate is filed with the local registrar of the district of death or as the state registrar directs. If items are missing at five days it is filed with what is available, and supplements follow.

steps.title: Local registrar transmits certificates to the state registrar
steps.who: Local registration officers, to the state registrar (Bureau of Vital Records and Health Statistics).
steps.summary: Local registrars forward all certificates to the state registrar, the custodian of the state's vital records, and keep local copies.

steps.title: Certified copies to applicants with direct and tangible interest
steps.summary: Copies go only to applicants with a direct and tangible interest; records become public 50 years after death. Each certified death certificate carries a $1 coroner-training surcharge.

steps.title: Monthly list of deceased residents to the Secretary of State
steps.who: The Department of Health and Welfare, to the Secretary of State.

deadline.text: on or about the 25th of each month, for the preceding month

steps.summary: Health and Welfare sends the name, date of birth, county and address of every Idaho resident who died in the preceding month, with SSNs and other identifiers. The Secretary of State also asks SSA monthly for death data.

steps.title: Secretary of State sorts by county; county clerks cancel deceased voters
steps.who: The Secretary of State, then each county clerk.
steps.trigger: Comparison of new and existing registrations, no later than 90 days before a statewide election.
steps.summary: The Secretary of State sends each county its list with eligibility information, and the county clerk must immediately cancel the registrations of voters reported as deceased.

steps.title: Copies to agencies for child support, child protection and fraud
steps.who: A state, federal or local public agency for child protection, child support enforcement or fraud investigation.
steps.trigger: A request, or the state registrar's own direction.
steps.summary: The state registrar must issue copies for these purposes, and may also let federal, state or municipal agencies use record data to verify their own data.

steps.title: National vital statistics agency gets copies free
steps.who: The state registrar, to the national agency in charge of vital statistics.
steps.summary: The national vital statistics agency may obtain copies or certifications of data without fee.

steps.title: Private bodies rely on certified copies
steps.who: A person with direct and tangible interest (family, estate representative).
steps.trigger: Need to prove the death to a private body.
steps.summary: State law has no death feed or check for banks or insurers, and no lists of registrations may be compiled for public use other than the voter-list exception. Private parties depend on certified copies.

registrationDeadlineDays.note: Five days after death. The mortician must also report to the local registrar within 24 hours of taking possession, for the disposition permit.

informantDuty.note: The person in charge of interment or removal of the body (the mortician or person acting as such) obtains and files the certificate.

medicalExaminerScrutiny.note: No independent review of all certificates. Coroner referral is limited to unattended, non-natural or no-certifier deaths, but the coroner must separately authorise every cremation.

electronicRegistration.note: Neither statute nor the IDAPA 16.02.08 rules read require electronic filing; filing is 'as prescribed by the State Registrar'. Whether Idaho's death registration system is fully electronic was not established from primary sources.

centralPopulationRegister.note: No population register; the state registrar is custodian of the vital records.

governmentPropagation.note: Under state law, Health and Welfare sends a monthly death list to the Secretary of State, and county clerks cancel those voters. Copies go on request to child support, child protection and fraud agencies. No statutory death feed to the Transportation Department (driver licences) or the State Tax Commission was found. Federal feeds such as SSA are in us-federal.

certificateAccess.note: Direct and tangible interest required; public after 50 years.

gaps: Pointer § 34-435 turned out to be the four-year non-voting purge, not death. Death-based cancellation is in § 34-433 (added 2025, ch. 276), which is cited instead.

No Idaho source was found for who may pronounce or determine death; Idaho's determination-of-death statute was not located. The guessed § 54-1819 404s, and the legislature's statute search (legislature.search.idaho.gov) returned no results to scripted queries. So no pronounce step is recorded.
Whether death certificates are filed electronically (an Idaho EDRS) is not stated in Title 39 chapter 2 or IDAPA 16.02.08, so electronicRegistration is null.

No statute was found requiring vital statistics to notify the Idaho Transportation Department (driver licences), the State Tax Commission or Medicaid of deaths. Without a working full-text search this is a negative from the chapters read (Title 39 ch. 2, Title 34 ch. 4), not from the whole code.
privateSectorVerification is deliberately left out of this file so that the us-federal value (LADMF/SSA) applies in the viewer. State law bars public lists of registrations (§ 39-270(c)).
Probate notice to creditors (public stage) was not researched.
